subject: frog
pitch: A red-eyed tree frog clinging to a leaf. Vivid lime-green skin, blue and cream striped flanks, orange toes with round sticky pads, a creamy white belly, and enormous ruby-red eyes with black slit pupils. It looks a little surprised, as if you just woke it up.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module scaled to a real red-eyed tree frog, with a thin leaf slab and stem as a prop beneath the frog sitting on top.

I'm sketching out the skeleton hierarchy -- pelvis, chest, neck, head, jaw -- then front and hind limb chains with shoulders, elbows, wrists, toes with pads, and hips, knees, ankles, feet with toes, oriented facing +Z.

Writing joint and limb helper functions...

Now I'm shaping the body as an ellipsoid with lime green countershading fading into a cream belly, and adding flank markings -- thin flattened stripe shapes in blue and cream positioned along the sides and thighs to mimic the frog's coloring.

Now I'm shaping the head and jaw as separate flattened ellipsoids, rounding the snout, then adding oversized bulging red eyes with vertical slit pupils angled forward and outward.

Still refining eye details...

For the surprised expression I'll add green upper eyelids as partial sphere caps that retract back since the eyes are wide open, mounted on the eye joints on the head. I'm also planning tiny dark nostril spheres at the snout, keeping the mouth simple since the separate jaw piece already conveys expression, and a cream-colored throat before moving on to the arms.

For the arm pose, I'm going with a frog-clinging stance: shoulders extend outward with upper arms angled back and forearms reaching forward-down to plant the hands on the leaf surface. The leaf itself will be a flat extruded slab in the XZ plane with a slight thickness, colored a deeper green with a darker midrib and vein details to add texture.

Continuing the arm down to wrist and hand, then fanning out four toes from the hand position at varying angles with short lengths ending in pads, each toe getting its own joint.

Now I'm setting up a mirrored naming scheme so the right-side limbs reuse the same structure as the left with flipped x-coordinates, keeping the rest pose neutral with limbs spread apart.

For the hind leg, I'm placing the hip, folding the thigh forward-outward in a frog-like crouch, and positioning the knee before working out the ankle joint.

I'll add a small blue-violet ellipsoid patch on the outer thigh with a cream stripe for color variation, and plan the toes and foot pads as orange capsules in two shades for contrast.

For the capsule helper, I'm settling on a signature that takes start/end points, radius, and an options object for color and bone assignment, with default tessellation sides around 8 for smooth but efficient geometry. I'm being careful with the joint helper to always pass parent explicitly rather than relying on auto-detection, since that risks picking the wrong nearest joint, and I'll support an optional aim target so bones can orient toward a direction.

I'm designing a chain helper that builds a sequence of joints along a polyline path, taking a parent, an array of names matching the points, and a role tag like 'arm' or 'leg' — for limbs this gives four named joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand tip), and for toes a shorter two-point chain with a 'digit' role, parented to the limb's final joint. Geometry capsules then reference these chain joints explicitly as their bones, and I'm sketching out the spine chain with a root joint at the origin feeding into a short path of pelvis-area points.

Continuing the chain concept into the spine (pelvis, chest, neck), head, jaw, and eye joints, I'm setting up limb parenting so arms attach to the chest joint and legs attach to the pelvis joint. Now I'm sketching the body geometry itself — a sphere scaled and positioned to form the torso, checking that it overlaps properly with the head, and applying a countershading paint pattern (lime to cream gradient) while confirming nonuniform scaling won't break the normals.

I'm deciding to share one countershaded paint between the head and jaw for consistency, then layering in a nested dorsal mottle pattern for added texture, confirming the paint-blending system handles nested color lists correctly. I'm also settling on smooth-shaded spheres rather than flat faceting for the body, and starting to work out stripe placement along the flank based on the body's center coordinates.

Working out flank stripe geometry...

I'll just default everything to chest for simplicity. For the head, I'm sizing the main head ellipsoid and adding a separate smaller ellipsoid for the lower jaw to give it definition.

Placing eyes on the sides of the head so they protrude slightly outward, and positioning the mouth opening at the front. For the pupils, I'm calculating a direction vector so they point slightly forward and down, then offsetting small pupil boxes from the eye centers along that direction with proper orientation.

That flat ring placement keeps failing the math, so I'll switch to a sphere-cap geometry oriented along the eye direction, which naturally hides edges inside the main eyeball.

Still placing eye details...

Adding small dark nostril spheres and a flattened tympanum disc behind the eye for extra realism, keeping the throat sac hidden under countershading. Now shifting to defining the leaf outline points.

Still adjusting leaf and stem geometry...

Working out the vein lengths and angles so they taper to match the leaf width at each point along the midrib, using a 55° rotation to angle them outward symmetrically. Veins stay mostly hidden under the frog body anyway, so I'm not fussing over precision. Thinking about adding a couple tiny translucent droplet spheres for a cute detail.

I'm mapping out the color scheme: lime-green limbs transitioning to orange hands and feet, cream stripes on the shins, blue accents on the outer thighs, with mottled coloring across the skin and leaf surface for texture. Defining the color palette constants now.

Writing frog builder skeleton...

Writing limb mirroring logic...

Computing toe directions outward with an angle offset for foot splay, then building each toe as a short chain capsule tapering from base to tip.

Adding a pad ellipsoid at each toe tip, then setting up hand base and wrist coordinates with toes fanning forward from the hand point at a spread angle, plus arm joint positions for the left limb.

Now I'm defining radii for the arm segments, marking the wrist-to-hand segment orange, placing the toe tips at a fixed height, and starting on the left leg joint coordinates and their radii.

Still placing thigh patches and joint offsets...

I'm computing overall frog height from eye and lid heights, checking it against the leaf dimensions to make sure proportions look right at real size.

Now I'm defining the eye geometry: positioning the eye sphere at its joint, building the eye cap as a partial sphere scaled down and oriented along the Y axis, and setting up the eyelid as a slightly larger hemisphere to check visibility from outside versus inside.

For the pupil, I'm creating a thin dark box oriented using the joint's direction vector so it forms a vertical slit shape with a helper function for adding scaled vectors. Then I'm starting to place small flattened spheres on the leaf to act as water droplets.
